description: Kubernetes service health for the PCA platform, keyed on workload (Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet) readiness to avoid per-pod churn; scaled-to-0 workloads are excluded. Shows which services are up/degraded now and historically, with Jobs/CronJobs and pod-level restart/crash detail handled separately. Edge collectors/sensors are out of scope.

options.content:
# PCA Service Health (Kubernetes)

Shows whether the PCA platform **services** running in the cluster are up now and when they were degraded/down. To stay stable and readable, the service timelines are keyed on the **workload** (Deployment / StatefulSet / DaemonSet), not individual pods – so a rollout that replaces pods does not create noise, and each row is a short, stable service name. Edge collectors/sensors are out of scope.

**Scaled-to-0 workloads are excluded** (desired replicas = 0, e.g. an optional app like latentapp when disabled) – they are intentionally off, not down, so they are not shown and not counted.

**How to read it**
- **Summary tiles**: fully-ready workloads vs total (scaled-to-0 excluded), degraded workloads, pending pods, crash-loops, restarts, failed jobs.
- **Per-group timelines**: each row is a workload's **ready/desired replica ratio** over time – GREEN (1) = fully ready, ORANGE = partially ready, RED (0) = no ready replicas (down), GAP = the workload did not exist or is scaled to 0. This is the authoritative 'is the service up / when was it down' view.
- **Jobs & CronJobs**: one-off/scheduled jobs are tracked separately (completed = normal; only failures are flagged).
- **Restarts & Crash-loops**: pod-level detail, filtered to pods that actually restarted or are stuck.

**Fixing a degraded/down service:** `kubectl describe` the workload and its pods (events: image pull, scheduling, probes), check pod logs, node pressure/resources, and upstream dependencies (e.g. if `postgres`/`zookeeper`/`kafka` is down, dependents go unready too).

Shows the Kubernetes cluster monitored by this deployment's Prometheus datasource.

**Filters:** `$namespace` scopes the board (namespace defaults to `pca`).

panels.description: Fully-ready workloads (Deployments + StatefulSets + DaemonSets with ready replicas >= desired, excluding any scaled to 0) shown as ready% plus ready/total. GREEN = everything at full capacity. ORANGE/RED = some/most services degraded – see 'Workloads degraded' and the per-group timelines.

targets.expr: 100 * ((count((kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0)) + (count((kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0)) + (count((kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0))) / ((count(kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0)))

(count((kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0)) + (count((kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0)) + (count((kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} >= kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"}) and (kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0)) or vector(0))

(count(kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"} > 0) or vector(0))

panels.title: Workloads ready

panels.description: Workloads with fewer ready replicas than desired (pods crashing, unschedulable, or unexpectedly scaled down). Scaled-to-0 workloads are not counted. RED = at least one service is not at full capacity – expand its functional group below.

targets.expr: (count(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace=~"$namespace"} < kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} < kube_statefulset_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) or vector(0)) + (count(kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{namespace=~"$namespace"} < kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{namespace=~"$namespace"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Workloads degraded

panels.description: Pods stuck in the Pending phase (cannot be scheduled or still initializing). RED = check node resources/affinity and the pod's events (`kubectl describe pod`).
panels.title: Pods pending

panels.description: Containers currently in CrashLoopBackOff. RED = a container keeps crashing on start – check its logs and config/dependencies (see Restarts & Crash-loops).
panels.title: CrashLoopBackOff

panels.description: Total container restarts in the namespace over the last 24h. A few are normal (rollouts/node moves); a steadily climbing count points at an unstable container – see Restarts & Crash-loops. (Informational.)
panels.title: Restarts (24h)

panels.description: Kubernetes Jobs currently reporting one or more failed pods (kube_job_status_failed > 0). RED = a batch/setup job failed – see Jobs & CronJobs. Completed jobs are normal and not counted.
panels.title: Failed jobs

panels.description: Container restarts per pod over the last hour, showing only pods that actually restarted (zero-restart pods are hidden to avoid rollout churn). Repeated bumps = a container crashing and being restarted – check that pod's logs and the waiting-reason panel below. NOTE: a Deployment rollout replaces pods with new names rather than restarting them, so a clean rollout shows nothing here; use the workload timelines above for rollouts/availability.
panels.title: Container Restarts (pods that restarted, 1h increase)

panels.description: When each pod was stuck in a container waiting-state for a genuine failure reason (benign PodInitializing/ContainerCreating excluded). A coloured block = the pod could not start during that time; a gap = not stuck. Row label shows the reason: ImagePull*/InvalidImageName = registry/credentials/tag; CrashLoopBackOff = app crashing on start; CreateContainerConfigError = bad config/secret/mount; CreateContainerError/RunContainerError = runtime problem. Check that pod's logs and `kubectl describe pod`.
panels.title: Pods Stuck Waiting (real failure reasons only)

panels.description: Ready/desired replica ratio over time for each workload in the 'Ingestion pipeline' group (Deployments/StatefulSets/DaemonSets whose name starts with one of: fedex, foxtrot, draftsman). GREEN = fully ready, ORANGE = partially ready, RED = no ready replicas (down), GAP = workload absent or scaled to 0. To fix a red/orange row: `kubectl describe` that workload and its pods, check events and logs, and any dependency it needs.
panels.title: Ingestion pipeline – workload readiness

Scaled-to-0 workloads are excluded. If a workload you expected in a named group appears here, its name differs from the service map – tell me and I'll add it. (Jobs/CronJobs are in the next section.)

panels.description: Kubernetes Jobs with failed pods or currently-active pods. GOOD: no 'failed' series (completed jobs just disappear – that is normal). BAD: a 'failed' series at >0 – that job's pod errored; check its logs. 'active' shows jobs currently running. One-off setup jobs and scheduled (CronJob) runs both surface here.
panels.title: Jobs – Failed / Active (by job)
